claims.claim: A general denial is allowed when the complaint in a limited civil case is unverified.
claims.quote: If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.
claims.note: This supports the type of denial, not eligibility to use a particular form.

claims.claim: PLD-050 is the short general denial form.
claims.note: The form is named but its text is absent.

claims.claim: PLD-050 may be used in any unverified limited civil case.
claims.note: The statute does not name PLD-050. The missing form's instructions are needed to check whether assignment and claim amount restrict its use.

claims.claim: The limited civil amount-in-controversy ceiling is $35,000, inclusive.
claims.quote: The amount in controversy does not exceed thirty-five thousand dollars ($35,000).
claims.note: The statutory measure excludes attorneys’ fees, interest, and costs.

claims.claim: A claim of $35,000 or less is, by that fact alone, a limited civil case.
claims.quote: an action or special proceeding shall be treated as a limited civil case only if all of the following conditions are satisfied:
claims.note: Subdivisions (b) and (c) also impose conditions on the relief sought.

claims.claim: A person who cannot afford the filing fee can request a fee waiver.
claims.note: No fee-waiver eligibility text is supplied.

claims.claim: Use FW-001 to request the waiver.

flags.text: “Any” extends a statutory rule about general denials to a particular form. The citation description mentions assigned claims over $1,000, but it is not the form text and does not establish the restriction's exact scope.
Relying on the unchecked PLD-050 instruction could lead to a defective response and risk default.

The stated scope includes verified complaints, but the draft gives no response option for them. Section 431.30(d) specifically requires positive or information-and-belief denials for verified claims assigned to a third party for collection.
The draft treats the $35,000 ceiling as a complete definition rather than one necessary condition.
Neither the clerk-specific filing instruction nor the FW-001 instruction is fully documented by the supplied texts.

result.summary: The sources support timely filing with the court and a general denial for an unverified complaint. They do not establish universal PLD-050 eligibility or the FW-001 instruction. The amount-only definition of a limited civil case conflicts with section 85.
